# Now 2.13.49
- Lyrics no longer move as one rigid block. Each line now starts travelling a beat after the line above it, so the stack settles like a chain of coupled springs instead of a single sliding panel, and a line change has some give to it. Where the lines end up is unchanged, so nothing drifts out of alignment once it comes to rest. - Line changes are interruptible. When lines come fast, each one retargets from wherever it currently is and carries its momentum into the next move rather than restarting. - Scrolling by hand now pins the lyrics where you left them, so a line change while you are reading elsewhere no longer drags the view away.

# Now 2.13.48
- The album art in the full screen view now responds to play and pause. Pausing settles it backward, with its shadow tightening as it goes; playing springs it forward again. Play bounces a little more than pause does, and both are interruptible, so tapping pause and then play immediately bends the motion from wherever it is rather than snapping back and starting over. - Scrolling the lyrics now hands control to you. The view stops chasing the line being sung, a "Back to current" button appears, and follow resumes on its own a few seconds after you stop. - The instrumental break marker breathes gently while it waits and scales away as the next line arrives, instead of sitting still and then vanishing.

# Now 2.13.47
- The dark app icon now sits on true black. It was previously a dark purple-grey, which read as washed out beside other dark-mode icons in the Dock. The warm glow behind the lit lyric line is unchanged.
